recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. If a future implementation guide establishes a reusable purchase-date or purchase-history pattern, open a new tracker for a concrete HL7 extension or extension-pack artifact rather than deriving one from FHIR-16488.
issue_request: FHIR-16488 requested a generic purchaseDate extension for Device, Substance, Medication, and similar product instances. The Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution instead directed clarification that implementation guides determine the relevant purchase date from DeviceRequest, SupplyRequest, DeviceDispense, SupplyDelivery, or similar resources, with local extension use only when a specific IG needs to copy a date.
initial_application: The issue was applied in bdf574e8931079285aa19c384dffd461c167a650 and merged through HL7/fhir#2183 as ea07a990e2, adding purchase-date guidance to DeviceRequest, SupplyRequest, DeviceDispense, and SupplyDelivery introduction/boundary text. Later commits FHIR-37980, FHIR-51689, and FHIR-53405 touched adjacent or same text without reversing the guidance.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively includes DeviceRequest, Device, Medication, and Substance in the current build; SupplyRequest, DeviceDispense, and SupplyDelivery directories exist but are not active resources in the current build. The active DeviceRequest page still contains the purchase-date guidance, and searches found no purchaseDate/purchaseHistory extension in active core product resources or the FHIR Extension Pack. Confluence minutes support the same rationale: purchase date is not per se a Device attribute, and any copy extension should be local until HL7 can define a clearer reusable scope.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current active source already tells implementers to determine purchase date through request, dispense, or delivery context, and adding a core extension or editing out-of-build pages would be broader than the approved issue and current build scope.
